title: An Observed Value Consistent Diffusion Model for Imputing Missing Values in Multivariate Time Series

problem.claim: Missing values hinder the utilization and interpretation of multivariate time-series data.

gap.claim: Existing approaches either fail to model imputation uncertainty or perform poorly in interpretability and accuracy because they ignore correlations between observed and missing values.

contributions.claim: The paper re-derives the Evidence Lower Bound for conditional diffusion models in the multivariate time-series imputation scenario.
The paper proposes MIDM, a multivariate imputation diffusion model with noise sampling, adding, and denoising mechanisms designed to maintain consistency between observed and missing values.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the derived ELBO and MIDM mechanisms as newly derived, novel, or newly designed contributions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on multivariate time-series imputation and forecasting show superiority of MIDM for generating conditional estimations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Missing values obstruct the use and interpretation of multivariate time-series data.
Existing methods use deterministic deep-learning imputations or sample multiple plausible imputations from a shared noise distribution.
These methods have shortcomings in uncertainty modeling, interpretability, and accuracy because they ignore correlations between observed and missing values.
The paper re-derives a conditional-diffusion ELBO and proposes MIDM with mechanisms intended to preserve observed-missing consistency.
The authors report superior conditional-estimation performance in imputation and forecasting experiments.

source_observation.claim: Observed and missing values are treated as correlated parts of samples from the same distribution.

interpretation.claim: Imputation methods may benefit from explicitly preserving relationships between observed and inferred components.

application.claim: When designing multivariate time-series imputation systems, incorporate observed-missing consistency into the probabilistic formulation and generation mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design generalizes beyond the reported imputation and forecasting tasks.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative experimental results are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational costs, or limitations.
